practiceNotes: This is a proposed curriculum. Completion of flashcard review does not certify proof, programming, laboratory or professional competence.
Use spaced retrieval for definitions, representations, assumptions, mechanisms and method selection; assess derivations, code, data analysis and experimental decisions separately with unseen tasks.
Programming work requires executable environments, version control and reproducible data/provenance records; benchmark claims require stated hardware and workloads.

Chemical, biological, electrical, laser and radiation experiments require appropriate facilities, supervision, risk assessment and institutional authorization. These conditions are not represented as already satisfied.
Use nonpathogenic teaching strains and nonhazardous substitutes where appropriate. Pathogen, animal, human-participant and genetic-engineering work requires relevant ethics and biosafety review.
Security exercises are restricted to owned or explicitly authorized sandbox systems. Robotics and control projects require physical safeguards or simulation.
Fieldwork requires permits where applicable, humane sampling, ecological impact controls and documented location/privacy practices.

Provided scientific software may support method use, but students must still justify assumptions, inspect diagnostics and distinguish supplied algorithms from implementations they can independently construct.
